title: SIB 2022-02R4 — GNSS outage and alterations
summary: Fourth revision of EASA's bulletin on GNSS jamming and spoofing. Interference keeps growing around the Baltic, Eastern Europe, the Black Sea, the Mediterranean, the Middle East and the Arctic. EASA recommends cross-checking position with non-GNSS means, reporting every event and considering anti-spoofing equipment. First published 3 July 2026 and re-issued with corrections on 22 July. Adds pilot–ATC phraseology and new training recommendations.
impact: Survey flight lines and trajectories depend on GNSS/IMU. Cover jamming and spoofing in SPO risk assessments and SOPs, especially for Nordic, Baltic and eastern campaigns.

title: ED Decision 2026/005/R — Airworthiness review process
summary: Updates the AMC and GM to Part-M, Part-ML, Part-CAMO, Part-CAO, Part-145 and Part 21 to support Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/100. Covers the airworthiness review, ARC and CofA processes, transfers between Member States and imports from outside the EU system.
impact: CAMOs managing survey aircraft must update procedures and exposition. Also changes how imported or foreign-registered aircraft come onto an EU register.

title: Joint action plan on GNSS interference
summary: Short, medium and long-term actions: coordinated monitoring across Europe, standard procedures and terminology for pilots and controllers, joint data analysis and clear responsibilities for ANSPs, operators and national authorities.
impact: Expect new NOTAM practices, ATC procedures and reporting duties for GNSS interference in affected FIRs.

title: Part-IS fully applicable (Reg. (EU) 2023/203)
summary: Organisations in scope, including air operators, CAMOs, Part-145 organisations and, per EASA's FAQ, declared SPO and NCC operators, must run an information security management system for cyber risks with a possible safety impact.
impact: A declared Part-SPO survey operator needs a Part-IS system alongside its existing management system. Flight-planning, data and GNSS toolchains are in the risk picture.

title: AIC NTL 01/26 — Coordination of civil activities
summary: Replaces AIC NTL 02/90, 05/20 and 01/25. Brings together the coordination rules for aerial work in controlled airspace and MoD reserved or restricted areas. Section 13 covers photography in ZRVF zones: request to CECAF, answer normally within about 15 working days, authorisation valid 12 months.
impact: This is now the rulebook for photogrammetric and LiDAR flights in Spain. The Spain card (last verified Aug 2025) says CECAF is contacted by RCC on your behalf — check whether that still holds.

title: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/100 — Airworthiness review and certificates
summary: Amends Regulations 748/2012 and 1321/2014 on the airworthiness review, airworthiness certificates and occurrence reporting. Adopted 15 January 2026, published in the Official Journal on 19 January, applicable since 7 August 2026.
impact: Changes how ARCs are issued and extended for C208, PA-31, P68 and DA42/62 fleets, and may widen the choice of who performs the review.

title: Opinion 01/2026 — Regular update of air operations rules
summary: Proposes amendments to Regulation 965/2012, including a new Subpart ORO.OCP on training of operations control personnel, a switch from ETOPS to EDTO and helicopter equipment changes. One-year general transition, three years for OCP training. The Commission draft based on it is expected to go to the committee vote in October 2026.
impact: Survey operators with a central dispatch or operations-control function may face new training obligations for that staff.

title: NPA 2025-12 — Continuing airworthiness regular update
summary: Proposes simplifying Regulation 1321/2014: deleting obsolete Part-M Subparts F and G, clarifying digital certificates and online applications and cutting rule material by about 20%. Consultation ran from 19 December 2025 to 30 April 2026; EASA has not yet published its Opinion.
impact: Maintenance expositions of survey fleets and their CAMO/Part-145 providers will need updating once adopted.

title: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2293 — Part-IS for declared organisations
summary: Amends Regulation 2023/203 for organisations operating under a declaration and corrects several aviation regulations, including Air Ops, FCL and continuing airworthiness.
impact: Sets the Part-IS obligations for declared operators such as Part-SPO survey companies.

title: NPA 2025-09 — SERA update and FF-ICE
summary: Proposes preliminary and electronic flight plans (eFPL) with unique flight identifiers, filing up to 120 hours before off-block, and 'N' in the SSR field when the transponder is unserviceable.
impact: Flight planning for cross-border survey missions will move to the new eFPL formats and procedures.

title: SERA package — Regs (EU) 2024/403, 404 and 405
summary: Revised radio-failure procedures (IFR wait 20 minutes instead of 7, new code 7601 when diverting), plus changes to emergency descent, speed deviation reporting, phraseology, special VFR and ATC clearances.
impact: Update lost-comms and contingency procedures in SOPs. Switzerland and the UK did not adopt these changes.

title: Permits to photograph defence and critical sites (Dz.U. 2025 poz. 432)
summary: Sets the procedure for permits to photograph or record about 25,000 marked defence and critical-infrastructure sites, including bridges, energy sites and ports. In force since mid-April 2025.
impact: Aerial imaging over marked Polish critical infrastructure may need a permit. There is no Poland card on the platform yet.

title: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1821 — Updated list of mandatory occurrence reports
summary: Updates the EU list of occurrences that must be reported. Adds categories for drones, U-space and information security (Part-IS) and removes some aviation-security occurrences. In force since 17 August 2026; the exact date the new categories apply is still to be confirmed.
impact: Update occurrence-reporting procedures, including information-security events and encounters with drones or U-space.

title: SIB 2026-09 — Inadequate protection of SBAS-based approach procedures
summary: Some SBAS-based instrument approaches may not give enough obstacle protection, especially in the missed approach, because procedure design and avionics standards do not match. Based on ICAO EB 2026/13, which asks states to reassess existing SBAS procedures.
impact: Survey aircraft flying SBAS/EGNOS approaches into regional airfields should watch for NOTAMs and amended procedures and brief crews on missed-approach risk.

title: SAIB-2026-16 — Elevator control system, King Air 100 series and Beech 99
summary: US bulletin republished by EASA on the elevator control system of King Air 100/A100/B100 and Beech 99 aircraft. Points to Beechcraft Mandatory Service Letter MTL-27-03.
impact: CAMOs managing King Air 100-series survey aircraft should check that MTL-27-03 is in the maintenance programme and has been done.

title: 2026 update of the EU dual-use control list (Regulation (EU) 2021/821, Annex I)
summary: The Commission adopted the annual replacement of the dual-use control list on 14 September 2026; it is now under scrutiny by Parliament and Council. It is not yet confirmed whether the entries for cameras, LiDAR or inertial navigation changed. Expected to enter into force around November 2026.
impact: Operators taking airborne cameras, LiDAR or high-grade IMUs outside the EU (for example to Serbia, North Macedonia or Montenegro) should re-check export classifications once it is published.

title: Flight time limitations for air taxi, emergency medical and single-pilot operations
summary: Extends EU flight and duty time rules to commercial air taxi, emergency medical and single-pilot aeroplane operations, replacing the old Subpart Q. Under scrutiny; most provisions would apply from 15 October 2028.
impact: Does not affect Part-SPO survey flights. It does affect survey companies that also hold an AOC for single-pilot or air-taxi flights.

title: AIC INT 07/26 — Transition to a centralised ARO
summary: ENAIRE is replacing the airport ARO offices with a single centralised ARO at Madrid ACC, open 24 hours. Flight plans can no longer be filed in person or by fax. The last phase runs from October to December 2026.
impact: Crews filing survey flight plans at Spanish airports must use the ENAIRE web client, phone or AFTN, and update their contact lists.
